headline: Google limits Meta's use of Gemini AI models due to compute capacity shortfall, report says
summary: Google reportedly limited Meta's access to its Gemini AI models due to insufficient computing capacity, disrupting some of Meta's internal AI projects.
details: Google informed Meta around March that it could not meet the full Gemini capacity Meta sought to purchase, according to the Financial Times. This shortfall has reportedly disrupted and delayed some of Meta's internal AI projects.

Meta was particularly impacted due to its exceptionally high demand for Google's models, though other Google clients have also been affected to a lesser extent. Reuters could not immediately verify the report, which cited people familiar with the matter.
As a result of these restrictions, Meta has encouraged its staff to be more efficient with AI tokens, which measure AI usage. This highlights a direct consequence for Meta's internal operations.

The incident underscores a broader industry challenge: despite billions spent on chips and data centers, companies struggle to secure enough computing power for growing AI services. Google Cloud's CEO Sundar Pichai noted that compute constraints limited higher growth and nearly doubled the cloud unit's backlog in Q1.

headline_marked: [[Qwythos-9B-Claude-Mythos makes 1M context windows a game changer]] for developer velocity
headline: Qwythos-9B-Claude-Mythos makes 1M context windows a game changer for developer velocity
summary: The Qwythos-9B-Claude-Mythos model demonstrates that 1M token context windows are now practical, enabling complex agentic workflows on local hardware. It shifts the focus from retrieval accuracy to reasoning across entire codebases.
details: For a long time, the 'million-token context window' was seen as a vanity metric, often leading to 'lost in the middle' retrieval decay. However, integrating this capability into a 9B parameter model like Qwythos-9B-Claude-Mythos shifts the focus to practical agentic workflows on local hardware.

Testing involved feeding Qwythos an entire codebase of a medium-sized Python project (roughly 150k tokens) along with architectural requirements. The goal was to assess its coherence and reasoning across disparate files.

Running the GGUF version via llama.cpp, Qwythos proved capable of connecting utility functions to logic errors without explicit pointers. This capability represents a significant boost for developer velocity in the 9B model class.

This approach transforms the problem from a search challenge to a reasoning one, allowing developers to feed entire relevant modules into a prompt. It eliminates the need for obsessive RAG chunk tuning.

Qwythos-9B-Claude-Mythos is a practical tool for practitioners, enabling the loading of a project, documentation, and conversation history into a single inference pass. This prevents the model from losing context and streamlines agent development.
